summary: Iguratimod is a conventional synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drug (csDMARD) that inhibits NF-kB signaling, reducing inflammatory cytokine and immunoglobulin production and suppressing osteoclast-driven bone destruction. Approved in Japan (Careram/Kolbet) and China (Iremod) for rheumatoid arthritis, it is given orally with a 4-week dose-escalation to limit early adverse effects, reaching a usual maintenance dose of 50 mg/day. It is NOT approved by the FDA or EMA. The most important safety concerns are serious gastrointestinal ulceration and bleeding, hepatic dysfunction, interstitial pneumonia, myelosuppression, and infection. Concomitant warfarin is contraindicated because iguratimod markedly enhances warfarin's anticoagulant effect, with reports of serious bleeding and death.

moa: Iguratimod is a low-molecular-weight csDMARD that inhibits activation of the transcription factor NF-kB. By blocking NF-kB signaling it suppresses the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines including IL-1beta, IL-6, IL-8, TNF-alpha, IL-17, and MCP-1, and reduces COX-2-mediated prostaglandin synthesis. It also inhibits immunoglobulin (antibody) production from B cells by acting on the protein kinase C and EGR1 pathways without depleting B cells, downregulates Th1/Th17 responses while upregulating regulatory T cells, and dose-dependently inhibits RANKL-induced osteoclast differentiation and bone resorption while promoting osteoblast differentiation. The net effect is reduced joint inflammation and protection against structural bone damage in rheumatoid arthritis.

absolute: Concomitant use of warfarin (risk of serious bleeding and death)
Pregnancy or women who may be pregnant
Active peptic ulcer or significant gastrointestinal ulceration
Serious blood disorders / significant bone marrow suppression
relative: History of peptic ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding
Hepatic dysfunction or elevated liver enzymes
History of or risk for interstitial pneumonia / pulmonary disease
Elderly patients (greater susceptibility to adverse effects)
monitor: Respiratory symptoms (cough, dyspnea) for interstitial pneumonia

preg: Contraindicated in pregnancy and in women who may be pregnant. Animal studies have shown reproductive toxicity. Women of childbearing potential should use effective contraception during treatment.
lact: Contraindicated during breastfeeding. The drug is excreted in milk in animal studies; women should not breastfeed while taking iguratimod.
renal: Specific dose adjustment is not well established; safety in significant renal impairment has not been adequately studied. Use with caution and monitor in patients with renal impairment.
hepatic: Contraindicated in severe hepatic impairment. Hepatic dysfunction (elevated transaminases, jaundice) is among the most common adverse reactions. Monitor liver function regularly and discontinue if significant abnormalities occur.

major: Warfarin - iguratimod markedly enhances the anticoagulant effect (increased PT-INR), with reports of serious bleeding and death; concomitant use is CONTRAINDICATED
Other anticoagulants/antiplatelet agents and NSAIDs - increased bleeding and GI ulceration risk
moderate: CYP2C9/CYP2C19 inhibitors (e.g., fluconazole) - may increase iguratimod exposure; monitor for adverse effects
Other DMARDs / immunosuppressants - additive immunosuppression and infection risk
Corticosteroids and other ulcerogenic drugs - increased gastrointestinal ulcer risk
minor: Drugs metabolized by CYP2C9 - iguratimod may affect their metabolism (basis of the warfarin interaction)
interactions.food: Take after meals; food enhances absorption without reducing bioavailability.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid excessive alcohol, which may compound the risk of hepatic injury and gastrointestinal irritation.
interactions.diagnostics: Can cause elevated liver transaminases and changes in coagulation parameters (PT-INR) when combined with warfarin; may cause cytopenias on blood counts.

serious: Serious infections (bacterial pneumonia, Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, sepsis)

monitoring: Liver enzymes at baseline and periodically
Complete blood count (white cells and platelets)
Respiratory symptoms and chest imaging if interstitial pneumonia suspected
Gastrointestinal symptoms and signs of bleeding
Coagulation parameters if any anticoagulant exposure

pearls: Not FDA- or EMA-approved; approved in Japan (Careram/Kolbet) and China (Iremod) - dosing here is from the approved Japanese/Chinese label
Concomitant warfarin is CONTRAINDICATED - iguratimod strongly potentiates warfarin (CYP2C9 interaction) with reported fatal bleeding
4-week dose escalation (25 mg/day then 50 mg/day) limits early adverse effects, which peak around week 4
Liver dysfunction and GI disorders are the most common adverse reactions; serious risks include GI ulcer/bleed, interstitial pneumonia, myelosuppression, and infection
Acts as a non-biologic DMARD by inhibiting NF-kB, suppressing cytokines and immunoglobulin production without depleting B cells
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered after a meal; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: There is limited information on iguratimod overdose. Excessive intake may intensify gastrointestinal effects, bleeding tendency, hepatic injury, and bone marrow suppression. Management is supportive with monitoring of liver function, blood counts, and coagulation; discontinue the drug and treat symptoms.
